transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-25 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jared, Priya, Carlos (Redwood); Mark, Lisa, Anita, Tom (Blue Harbor)
---
Summary: quick intake between procurement/legal/security and Redwood to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing band for pilot and reserved capacity options. Customer concerned about data residency, KMS, and audit logs. Redwood AE/SE clarified hosted vs private deployment tradeoffs and proposed pilot metrics.
Topics discussed: MSA redlines, DPA exceptions, SLA latency and uptime commitments, KMS/HSM options, SSO/SAML, pricing for pilot vs Dedicated reserved pools, procurement timeline and approval gates.
---
00:00 Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jared from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya our solutions engineer and Carlos on success. How's everyone?
00:12 Mark: Hey Jared, good thanks. Busy week. Appreciate you squeezing this in.
00:18 Lisa: Hi — Lisa O'Connell from legal. I'll be the MSA redline owner.
00:24 Anita: Anita from infosec, quick heads up, we'll want encryption, key management, and auditability spelled out.
00:31 Priya: Great, thanks. Agenda — we'll run through the MSA/DPA redline path, SLA asks and then technical constraints for pilot. Sound OK?
00:40 Tom: Works for finance — I mainly want to understand pricing delta between hosted API and Redwood Dedicated.
00:48 Jared: Perfect. Quick contextual note: Redwood provides hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and an on‑prem/private option. For most pilots, customers start hosted and then move to Dedicated once throughput/costs need predictability.
01:05 Mark: So our high level — we need PII redaction and to guarantee no customer data leaves EU regions for now. Also timeline: procurement approval by mid‑September to start pilot late September.
01:18 Priya: Cool. On the data residency piece, we have region pinning in the hosted product and a Private VPC option if you need customer‑controlled networking. There is also an on‑prem bundle if the compliance bar requires it.
01:34 Lisa: From legal — the DPA has two exceptions we typically ask: log retention max and subprocessors list. We want guaranteed 90 day deletion on request and full subprocessor disclosure plus 30 days notice before changes.
01:46 Jared: We can typically do 90 days for certain datasets, but need to flag that model training/embedding caching uses ephemeral caches — Priya can explain the KV cache and how long we retain token prefixes.
01:58 Priya: Right, uh, so the runtime keeps prefix cache for performance — that's K V cache, sometimes mmm, the transcript says K V cash lol — but in practice we can control cache eviction and not persist PII. For the pilot we can enable aggressive TTL so nothing persists beyond 24 hours, and we can show config.
02:22 Anita: Will you integrate with customer KMS? We require BYOK/HSM or a managed KMS with control plane integration.
02:30 Priya: Yes, we have KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and support HSM via customer network for Private). For hosted BYOK we support envelope encryption, and keys are never in the clear in Redwood control plane.
02:46 Lisa: And audit logs — we need tamper‑evident logs for admin actions and a trail for data access.
02:53 Carlos: On the console side we can provide per‑route logs, token‑level cost breakdowns and an audit trail. Retention policy can be adjusted per contract — longer retention is treated as an add‑on.
03:10 Tom: Pricing question: what's the delta to buy a 3 month Dedicated burst pool vs staying hosted with reserved commitment?
03:20 Jared: Very common. Hosted is usage-based, great for fast start. Dedicated is monthly commit for predictable throughput. For a three month pilot — we typically recommend a short reserved buffer or purchase committed vGPU hours. I'll send a pricing worksheet with both scenarios.
03:34 Mark: We'd like to see a cost-per-100k tokens estimate at 2x latency targets and at 8k context.
03:42 Priya: We'll model that. Also note quantization/ lower‑precision runtimes change costs — we can recommend model variants.
03:50 Lisa: Back to MSA — we're pushing for indemnification language and IP carveouts. Can Redwood accept standard mutual indemnities and limit of liability tied to fees?
04:03 Jared: Standard mutual indemnities are ok; liability caps usually tied to 12 months fees for pilots but can be negotiated for enterprise. We'll flag this for legal.
04:12 Anita: One more security item — we want to run a short SCA/pen test or at least get a security questionnaire answered within the 2 week procurement window.
04:22 Priya: We can share our security pack: SOC 2 Type II, ISO docs, pen test summary. We also have a security questionnaire template we can fill.
04:29 Lisa: Great. We'll send the redlines — there are three specific MSA asks: data deletion clause, subprocessors notice, and cross‑border transfer clause.
04:39 Jared: Understood. We'll track those.
04:44 Mark: Timeline check — procurement signoff mid‑Sep, pilot kickoff late Sep, go/no‑go for Dedicated decision end of Oct. Is that realistic?
04:54 Priya: That looks fine — pilot metrics should be latency P95 < 350ms for simple prompts and success rate > 98% for completions, but we'll align to your exact SLAs.
05:07 Tom: On billing — we want a T&E estimate first for approval and then a firm quote after scope defined. Is that ok?
05:15 Jared: Absolutely. We'll do an initial cost estimate and then a formal quote tied to the pilot spec.
05:21 Lisa: On subprocessors — we may require a right to object within 30 days. Is that something Redwood allows?
05:30 Jared: We typically provide notice windows; right to object is doable for critical subprocessors with remediation plan. We'll note that.
05:37 Anita: For keys — for the private option, will you support customer‑managed rotation and HSM attestation?
05:45 Priya: Yes, rotation and attestation are supported; we'll surface the exact flows in the security doc.
05:50 Jared: Ok I'm going to summarize next steps — we'll send redlined MSA/DPA within 3 business days, Priya to send pilot SLO doc and pricing worksheet, Carlos to set up a pilot onboarding checklist, and Anita/Lisa to send specific artifact list and redlines.
06:08 Mark: Sounds good. Any other blockers?
06:12 Lisa: One question — export controls and data residency in EU. We'll add a clause.
06:18 Priya: We can support region pinning and contractual language for EU data processing.
06:23 Jared: Great. We'll also include an optional SLA uplift for Dedicated if you need 99.95% vs hosted default.
06:32 Tom: We'll expect a formal estimate by Sep 2 to route through finance.
06:36 Carlos: I'll propose Sep 8 for technical kick off — Priya and Anita to run test harness and sample inference loads.
06:44 Mark: Sep 8 works for ops.
06:47 Lisa: I'll try to get redlines in by Aug 29.
06:52 Jared: Thanks everyone. We captured action items and will follow up.
06:58 [meeting ends] 
---
